:::{#exm-bernoulli-precision-deriv}
#### Derivative of the precision at $\prob = 1/4$

At $\prob = 1/4$, the precision is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\precision
&= \frac{1}{\prob(1 - \prob)}
&& \text{(definition of $\precision$)}\\
&= \frac{1}{\frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{3}{4}}
&& \text{(substitute $\prob = 1/4$)}\\
&= \frac{16}{3}
&& \text{(multiply the fractions and take the reciprocal)}
\end{aligned}
$$

so by @lem-bernoulli-precision-deriv,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\prob} \precision
&= -\sqf{\precision} \paren{1 - 2 \prob}
&& \text{(@lem-bernoulli-precision-deriv)}\\
&= -\sqf{\paren{\frac{16}{3}}} \paren{1 - \frac{1}{2}}
&& \text{(substitute $\precision = 16/3$ and $\prob = 1/4$)}\\
&= -\frac{256}{9} \cdot \frac{1}{2}
&& \text{(square and subtract)}\\
&= -\frac{128}{9}
&& \text{(multiply the fractions)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The precision falls as $\prob$ rises toward $1/2$, where it is smallest, which matches the negative sign.

:::
